clue.text: The lack of runs, in the end

indicators.note: in places the run abbreviation inside the word for the end

parts.note: death is the end of life
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A batting side scores nothing, right down to the final over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the end' reads as a time phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'the end' is DEATH.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearth is a scarcity or shortage, a lack of something.

clue.text: Set off for assignation outside school

indicators.note: outside says the word for an assignation goes round the school

parts.note: an assignation is a date, a romantic meeting
Eton is the famous English public school

explanation.surface: Someone leaves for a secret rendezvous beyond the school gates.
explanation.walkthrough: ETON College is an English boarding school near Windsor.
explanation.definitionFit: To detonate a bomb is to set it off, triggering its explosion.

clue.text: Any crest that's developed for a blood line

indicators.note: developed suggests the letters of any crest have been worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A family coat of arms is designed to proclaim an aristocratic lineage.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is one's line of descent, the family lineage traced through blood.

clue.text: Informed that the bells rang loudly

indicators.note: loudly signals that the words are to be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: bells that rang slowly were tolled

explanation.surface: Someone is told that the church bells pealed out at full volume.
explanation.definitionFit: To be informed of something is to have been told it.

clue.text: Leather throw with fleece

parts.note: a horse that throws its rider is said to buck
to fleece someone is to cheat them, to skin them

explanation.surface: A leather jacket is tossed on together with a woolly jumper.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckskin is soft leather made from deer or sheep hide.

clue.text: Current diets designed to be accessible to all

indicators.note: designed indicates the letters of current diets are arranged into a new pattern

explanation.surface: Fashionable eating plans are made to suit everybody.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with no limits placed on it is open, available to everyone.

clue.text: Acknowledged that it sounded fresh

indicators.note: sounded says the word for fresh is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: fresh means new

explanation.surface: Someone admits that an idea rang original.
explanation.definitionFit: Acknowledged in the sense of was aware of, recognised: past tense of know.

clue.text: Vulgar school with superior equipment

indicators.note: superior means placed above, so in this down clue the equipment sits on top of the school

parts.note: kit is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A common sort of school boasts better facilities than it deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Kitsch is tasteless, garish art or decoration, so vulgar in style.

clue.text: Agreed it was peculiar in Edward's case

indicators.note: Edward's case means the name serves as a casing around the other word

parts.note: Ned is a short form of Edward
peculiar means odd

explanation.surface: People concurred that there was something strange about Edward's legal affair.
explanation.definitionFit: Nodding the head is a gesture of assent, so nodded means agreed.

clue.text: An amusing way to catch fish?

definitions.text: An amusing way to catch fish?

parts.words: An amusing way to catch fish?
parts.note: trout can be caught by stroking them gently by hand, the same word as the light touch that makes a person laugh

explanation.definitionFit: Tickling makes people laugh, and tickling trout is an old poacher's method of catching them by hand.

clue.text: Stopped a run, and relaxed

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
relaxed means rested

explanation.surface: A batsman pauses after one run and takes it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrested means halted, as when growth or a fall is arrested.

clue.text: Colleague fixed poker, etc

parts.note: a colleague is a companion or associate
fixed means set

explanation.surface: A fellow worker has rigged a card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A companion set is a stand of fireside tools: poker, tongs, brush and shovel.

clue.text: The issue reverts to hot food

indicators.note: reverts means the word for issue turns back on itself

parts.note: issue means offspring, a son
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: The topic returns to a discussion of warm meals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a topic, but it means offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is informal British slang for grub, something to eat.

clue.text: Price paid to cross a beach, perhaps

indicators.note: to cross means the price goes across, round, the single letter

parts.note: the price paid is the cost

explanation.surface: Someone pays a fee for passage over the sands.
explanation.definitionFit: A beach is one example of shoreline, the land beside the sea.

clue.text: Top bill? I object!

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
the first-person pronoun in its object form is me

explanation.surface: Someone protests at the headline charge on an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I object!' looks like a protest, but it means the object case of I.
explanation.definitionFit: Acme means the peak or highest point of achievement.

clue.text: Hot drink companies start advertising

parts.note: two companies give CO twice

indicators.note: start indicates taking the opening letter of advertising

explanation.surface: Firms begin promoting a warming beverage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate beverage made from cacao powder.

clue.text: Exploiting America with one? No good!

parts.note: US stands for the United States of America
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A complaint that the United States, taking advantage with an ally, behaves badly.
explanation.definitionFit: Using someone means taking advantage of them, exploiting them.

clue.text: Sharpe's different way of expressing things?

parts.note: the name Sharpe is a rearrangement, a turn, of the word for an expression

explanation.surface: The fictional soldier Sharpe has an unusual manner of speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: Sharpe is a fictional British army hero; his name is a different arrangement of the six letters of the phrase's last word.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn of phrase is a distinctive manner of expression in words.

clue.text: Passion supporting late tie

indicators.note: supporting means placed beneath, so in this down clue the passion sits below

parts.note: late means dead, as in the late king
heat is passion, as in the heat of the moment

explanation.surface: Fervent backing for a draw scored at the last minute.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead heat is a race where competitors finish exactly level, a tie.

clue.text: Hip individual who's actually there?

parts.note: hip means fashionable, in
an individual is a person

explanation.surface: A trendy figure who really shows up at events.
explanation.definitionFit: Being present in person means physically attending, not by proxy.

clue.text: Worry that follows departure from thriving business

indicators.note: that follows means the worry is placed after the departure

parts.note: going means leaving, departure
concern is worry

explanation.surface: Anxiety sets in after someone quits a flourishing firm.
explanation.definitionFit: A going concern is a business operating profitably and expected to continue.

clue.text: Gin is taken from dining-car — that's bad, really bad!

indicators.note: bad signals that what remains of dining-car after gin goes is jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the gin has been removed from the restaurant car of a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is taken from' removes the letters G, I, N from DININGCAR, leaving DINCAR; 'bad' rearranges those.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancid describes stale, rotten food or fat, so very unpleasant or nasty.

clue.text: A pair of fives — error raised game

parts.note: two fives make ten

indicators.note: raised means the word for error is turned upwards in this down clue

parts.note: a sin is a moral error

explanation.surface: Two fives make a slip in a match of cards or dice.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis is a racket sport played over a net.

clue.text: More courageous, but not British, say

indicators.note: not says the abbreviation for British is dropped

parts.note: more courageous means braver

explanation.surface: Someone claims the bolder hero was foreign.
explanation.definitionFit: To aver is to assert or declare something firmly.

clue.text: Listening to maxims that cause injuries

indicators.note: listening to means the word for maxims is to be heard spoken, in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: saws are proverbs or maxims

explanation.surface: Hearing old proverbs that wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Sores are painful patches of damaged skin, so a kind of wound.

clue.text: Afraid, left with nothing to do

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Afraid, left with nothing to do' (4) for IDLE: 'with nothing to do' defines it, but no reading of 'Afraid, left' builds the letters; the clue may be garbled.
annotationWithheld.clue: Afraid, left with nothing to do

clue.text: Getting the pip, we hear? So give up!

indicators.note: we hear says the word for pip is to be heard, not read

parts.note: a pip is a seed

explanation.surface: Someone who gets annoyed is told to surrender.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the pip' looks like the British idiom for being irritated, but pip is a fruit seed.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to surrender or yield something.

clue.text: Sailor provides check on board

definitions.meaning: a ship's officer below the master
chess's winning attack on the king played on the board

explanation.surface: A seaman keeps watch on deck.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant ship's officer is a mate, and checkmate in chess is shortened to mate.

clue.text: Speak against poetry

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
verse is poetry

explanation.surface: Someone argues against poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: To converse is to talk, to hold a conversation.

clue.text: Press for written examinations

definitions.meaning: the separate written tests in an exam

explanation.definitionFit: The press means newspapers, and exam papers are the written tests sat by students.

clue.text: They could be consumed when suffering from tension on the way back

indicators.note: on the way back says the word for tense is read in reverse

parts.note: suffering from tension means stressed

explanation.surface: Anxious travellers comfort-eat on the return journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Desserts are puddings, things eaten at the end of a meal.

clue.text: Floored by diatribe — a tendency to conceal it

indicators.note: a tendency to conceal it says the run of letters is concealed within the words

explanation.surface: Someone is knocked flat by a rant that tends to hide its true point.
explanation.definitionFit: Floored means knocked down, defeated, as in beaten.
